summary: Key insights from our BTH degree thesis investigating how structured prompt engineering can make Test-Driven Development more accessible and effective.

title: Pipeline Observability: Automated Health & Alerting with OpenTelemetry
summary: Why internal delivery pipelines deserve first-class telemetry, distributed tracing, and automated failure detection.
content:
### The Hidden Cost of Opaque Pipelines

Modern software delivery relies heavily on complex CI/CD environments with multi-stage build matrices, test executions, and automated deployments. Yet when a pipeline fails or slows down, developers often spend hours digging through thousands of lines of unformatted console logs.

### Treating CI/CD as a Distributed System

By applying observability best practices to our delivery infrastructure, we gain instantaneous visibility into execution health:

* **Distributed Tracing for Builds:** Modeling each pipeline stage, container initialization, and test runner as spans in an OpenTelemetry trace.
* **Automated Failure Fingerprinting:** Parsing failure traces to automatically categorize flaky tests, environment timeouts, or genuine code regressions.
* **Real-Time Notification Flows:** Routing rich context notifications directly to engineering channels so teams can remediate issues before blocking releases.

```yaml
# OpenTelemetry trace instrumentation snippet for pipeline steps
- name: Run Test Suite with Telemetry
  env:
    OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: "http://collector:4317"
    OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: "ci-pipeline-runner"
  run: |
    ./run-tests-with-telemetry.sh
```

Observability transforms CI/CD from a black box into an intelligent, self-monitoring delivery platform.

title: Architecting Developer-First AI Platforms & Go CLI Tooling
summary: Building automated workflows for validating, versioning, and publishing reusable AI agents and skills.
content:
### Moving Beyond Ad-Hoc Prompts

As AI capabilities integrate deeper into engineering workflows, managing agent configurations, custom skills, and prompt templates in unstructured files quickly becomes unmaintainable.

To scale AI tools across teams, we need **developer platforms** that treat AI resources with the same rigor as production code.

### Core Platform Architecture

1. **Declarative Schemas:** Defining AI agent capabilities, allowed tool groups, and system prompts in validated YAML/JSON specifications.
2. **Automated CI Validation:** Running automated verification pipelines to lint prompt schemas, check model version compatibility, and run regression evals on every commit.
3. **Go-Based Developer CLI:** Providing engineers with a blazing-fast, cross-platform CLI tool for scaffolding, testing, and publishing agents to a central registry.

```bash
# Example CLI command for validating and publishing an AI skill
$ ai-platform skill validate ./skills/code-review
✔ Schema valid
✔ 12 test evaluations passed
$ ai-platform skill publish ./skills/code-review --version v1.2.0
```

When AI tooling feels native, fast, and version-controlled, engineering teams can build reliable workflows with confidence.

title: The Renaissance of Zero-Build Static Web Craftsmanship
summary: Why returning to semantic HTML5, modern CSS custom properties, and native ES modules brings joy back to web development.
content:
### The Power of Simplicity

For years, the default expectation for creating any website was configuring complex bundlers, node_modules with thousands of transitive dependencies, and brittle build scripts.

Today, modern web standards provide everything needed for building stunning, highly responsive websites out of the box:

* **CSS Custom Properties & Grid:** Native design systems and responsive layouts without preprocessors.
* **Zero Runtime Overhead:** Browsers download raw, clean assets directly with 0ms compilation lag.
* **Longevity:** A zero-dependency static page built with web standards will render identically 10 years from now without broken dependency trees.

True craftsmanship often lies in choosing what to leave out.
